At 25X magnification, Saturn may look elongated or appear to have tiny “ears.”", "reason": "The page confirms Saturn's rings can be seen through a modest backyard telescope (4.5-inch Dobsonian) and mentions 25X view, and notes Saturn was about 845 million miles away, though it says rings are easier to distinguish at 50X rather than clearly resolved at 25X."}

parsed.note_claim: Saturn's rings can be seen with a small amateur telescope (the note says at just 25x magnification), even though Saturn is hundreds of millions of miles away.
parsed.label: SUPPORTS
parsed.quote: That affordable telescope had enough aperture and magnification to clearly show the rings in all their glory. ... At 25X magnification, Saturn may look elongated or appear to have tiny “ears.”
parsed.reason: The page confirms Saturn's rings can be seen through a modest backyard telescope (4.5-inch Dobsonian) and mentions 25X view, and notes Saturn was about 845 million miles away, though it says rings are easier to distinguish at 50X rather than clearly resolved at 25X.
